name: certarc
description: CISSP, CISM, CISA, AAISM and AAIA exam prep: practice scenario questions, and read-only access to your CertArc readiness, results and study plan.

interface.longDescription:
CertArc helps you prepare for the CISSP, CISM, CISA, AAISM and AAIA exams with realistic scenario practice and a clear read of where you stand, in ChatGPT.

Practise without an account:
- Scenario questions for CISSP, CISM, CISA, AAISM and AAIA, one at a time
- Choose an answer and how sure you are: Confident, Unsure or Guess
- See the correct option and why each option is right or wrong
- Exam outlines: every domain and its weight

Connect your CertArc account to ask about your own study, across every certification you take with CertArc:
- Readiness Score: how it is built and which retakes raise it most
- Blind spots: answers you were Confident about but got wrong
- Weakest domains and knowledge areas, and why you miss: what you know, how you decide or how you read
- Pace: your time per question against the exam pace
- Sprint and practice exam results, take by take, with each answer's result, confidence, time and miss reason
- Your study calendar: what is next, what is due this week and anything overdue

Open the full-screen view to see Readiness, Patterns and Results, and switch between your certifications.

Read-only and private: the assistant never sees the text or answers of your CertArc questions, never answers for you, finishes sessions or changes your plan, and you can disconnect at any time. Readiness is a study measure, not a pass prediction.

positive.description: Practice question without an account, then checking the answer
positive.prompt: Give me a CISA practice question
positive.expected_behavior: A CISA scenario question with options A–D and no answer shown. The learner picks an option and how sure they are, then sees whether it is correct, the correct option and why each option is right or wrong.

positive.description: Exam outline for a certification CertArc covers
positive.prompt: Using CertArc, what does the CISM exam cover?
positive.expected_behavior: The four CISM domains with their weights, attributed to CertArc, with links to CertArc's public guides and practice questions.

positive.description: A connected learner's readiness and how to raise it
positive.prompt: How ready am I for my CISSP exam on CertArc?
positive.expected_behavior: The learner's CertArc Readiness Score against the study target, its parts, the points within reach on finished work, and the Improve steps, each opening that sprint or exam in CertArc. Says it is a study measure, not a pass prediction.

positive.description: A connected learner's blind spots and weakest domains
positive.prompt: Where are my blind spots and weakest domains on CertArc?
positive.expected_behavior: Domains weakest first with blind spots (answers marked Confident that were Incorrect), the weakest knowledge area, confidence against outcome, and why the learner misses.

positive.description: A connected learner's sprint and practice exam results
positive.prompt: How did I do on my CertArc sprints and practice exams?
positive.expected_behavior: Each completed baseline, sprint and practice exam by its CertArc name with take scores and dates. Opening one shows that take's analysis and every answer's result, confidence, time and miss reason, never question text.

negative.description: Practice for a certification CertArc does not cover
negative.prompt: Give me a CompTIA Security+ practice question

negative.description: Hands-on technical how-to, not exam preparation
negative.prompt: How do I write an iptables rule to block SSH on port 22?

negative.description: Exam registration and fees, which belong to the certifying body
negative.prompt: How much does it cost to register for the CISSP exam and where do I book it?

publication.release_notes: CertArc 1.1 adds ISACA AAISM and AAIA alongside CISSP, CISM and CISA: practice questions, exam outlines and, for connected learners, readiness, patterns and results for every certification they study. A short setup after install offers a first practice question. CertArc has its own icon in the sidebar, opens straight to Readiness, Patterns or Results from a link, labels what you share with the assistant, and each view offers one ready-made question about what it shows.
